transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Honestly, it’s my sleep. That’s what finally made me call the employee assistance program. I’m barely sleeping right—I lie there replaying work stuff and arguments at home, then I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and can’t really get back to sleep. I start the day feeling like I never actually rested.
How long has this trouble with sleep been going on, and does it seem to happen even when things are going relatively well for you?

It’s been about a year and a couple months now. It really started when the arguments at home got a lot worse. As for when things are going okay… I guess it’s hard to say, but the sleep problem has pretty much stuck around since then.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively or feeling anxious about things even when there’s not an immediate problem, and does it feel hard to control that worry?

I’m not really sure. I do worry, mostly when there’s something specific going on, like work or stuff at home. I don’t know if I’d say it’s constant or out of nowhere. It can be hard to shut off at night, but I’m not sure beyond that.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried even when there isn’t anything specific going on, like when you’re alone or things are calm at home and work?

I don’t know if I’ve really noticed that. If things are actually calm, I’m not usually sitting there feeling anxious for no reason. It’s more when something is going on or I’m thinking about something that happened.
Have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, even when the stress from work or home isn’t on your mind?

Yeah… I think so. Most days there’s this kind of heavy, gray mood that just follows me around, from work to the car and then home. Even when nothing specific is happening, I still feel kind of hollow.

When you say your mind is replaying work stuff and arguments at home at night, does that feel like something you can’t stop, even when you try, or is it more that those thoughts just come up naturally when you’re trying to wind down?

It feels pretty hard to stop once I’m in it. I’ll try to wind down, but I just end up lying there going over work stuff or arguments at home. A lot of nights I wake up around 3 or 4 and then I’m basically done sleeping. That’s actually what pushed me to call the employee assistance program — I’m starting the day feeling like I never really rested.

Do you find yourself getting really worried or stressed out about small, everyday things — like chores, minor responsibilities, or even things that haven’t happened yet — even when there’s no big reason to be upset about them?

Not really, no. I mean, I get stressed when there’s an actual reason, but I haven’t noticed myself getting really worked up over small chores or things that haven’t happened yet. It’s not like constant worry about every little thing.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or like you don’t have any energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally taxing?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do feel worn out sometimes, but I haven’t clearly noticed it being most days or when I haven’t done much. It’s not the main thing I’ve been tracking, I guess.
Have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy, even when things at home or work aren’t particularly stressful?

Yeah… I have. I used to really look forward to stuff like pickup basketball, bowling nights, going to music festivals, even having friends over and using the smoker. Lately I either cancel, or if I do go, I feel like I’m just kind of there, going through the motions. It doesn’t really feel fun the way it used to.
Have you noticed that it's harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly most days, even when you're not particularly stressed or tired?

Yeah, I have noticed that. At work especially. I used to be able to knock out sales forecasts or client decks pretty quickly, but now I’ll sit there reading the same slide over and over, like five times, and still feel unsure. I second-guess the numbers, second-guess what I’m trying to say, and it takes me way longer to make a simple decision.
